card.name: Latin dance
card.era: Term formalized 20th century; roots Indigenous/European/African colonial era
card.tagline: Umbrella term for many Latin American social and ballroom dances.
card.profile: 'Latin dance' is a broad umbrella category, not a single dance. It has two meanings: (1) social/street Latin dances (salsa, mambo, merengue, rumba, bachata, bomba, plena) and (2) the competitive ballroom 'International Latin' category (cha-cha-cha, samba, rumba, paso doble, jive). It draws on Indigenous American, European, and African influences (English Wikipedia). Argentine folk dances (chacarera, gato, zamba) are generally NOT classed as 'Latin dance.'
card.insight: As a category, 'Latin dance' reflects the fusion of Native, European, and African traditions across Latin America and the codification of competitive ballroom Dancesport (English Wikipedia).

lessons.title: Zumba® Latin Easy-To-Follow Basic Steps Tutorial for Beginners

parts.note: Instructors introduce themselves and welcome beginners to the basic steps tutorial.
Teacher introduces the first rhythm, Cumbia, and explains the basic bounce and footwork.
Teacher leads Cumbia basic steps and variations with counting and arm movements.
Teacher introduces Merengue rhythm with marching in place.
Teacher demonstrates Merengue march and 6-count variations with partner.
Teacher transitions to Salsa rhythm, introducing the basic tap and front-and-back steps.

steps.name: Cumbia Two-Step
steps.description: Stepping in place with a slight back foot bend and bounce.

steps.name: Cumbia Front and Back
steps.description: Stepping forward and backward with alternating foot taps.

steps.name: Merengue March
steps.description: Marching in place while letting the upper body sway.

steps.name: Merengue Six-Count
steps.description: Side-to-side steps counted up to six with arm movements.

steps.name: Salsa Front and Back
steps.description: Stepping front and back with simple weight shifts.
